title: Fourier norm and decision tree size
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f$ be a function from the $n$-dimensional sign cube to $\\{\pm1\}$, and let $T$ be a finite binary decision tree whose queries use coordinates from a fixed subset of the $n$ coordinates and whose leaves are real numbers. If evaluating $T$ on the binary encoding of each sign vector gives the real-valued version of $f$, then the Fourier one-norm of that real-valued function is at most the number of leaves of $T$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a sign-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
$T$ is a decision tree over a subset of the coordinates with real-valued leaves
$T$ computes the real-valued version of $f$ on binary-encoded inputs
